previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and poor oral intake. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain control. Due to inability to advance beyond clear liquids, a PICC line was placed on hospital day 9, and TPN was initiated. Her pain gradually improved, and she remained stable without complications. She was discharged home on TPN with home health support, continuing her baseline medications and follow-up plans with primary care and gastroenterology. Lab monitoring included stable but low WBC and mild anemia, with transient hypophosphatemia corrected during the stay.

Brief Hospital Course:
Pleasant ___ yo F with hx of chronic idiopathic pancreatitis, now 
admitted for acute exacerbation.
  
# Acute on Chronic Pancreatitis: Pt presented with pain and 
nausea which she described as consistent with prior pancreatitis 
flares. However, unlike prior flares, her amylase and lipase 
were not noted to be elevated. Her exam on presentation was not 
concerning for acute abdomen and CT scan done at last admission 
to ___ showed pancreatic stranding but no e/o 
pseudocyst or necrosis. On admission, she was made NPO and 
placed on PRN dilaudid along with IV fluids.  With this therapy, 
she slowly improved over one week and upon discharge, was able 
to tolerate a regular diet and po medications.  She is being 
discharged with close follow-up with her PCP and GI and a 
limited supply of pain medications, with instructions to taper 
as the pain resolves. 

# Anemia: History of iron deficiency and B12 deficiency. No e/o 
active bleeding. Hct stable.
